parts.text: The Discovery was still trapped in the ice and, with winter closing in, Scott ordered that Shackleton return to New Zealand when the Morning

northwards on March 2 1903. Among polar historians, Scott’s decision has been controversial. Some suggest that Scott saw Shackleton as a potential rival, though there isn’t a great deal of evidence for this.

Early return and
So, Shackleton’s career as a polar explorer seemed to have got off to a bad start. While Scott sent him back with a glowing reference, he had been pronounced unfit for further Antarctic

. Frustratingly, he seemed “practically well” according to Gerald S Doorly, then a junior officer on the Morning, by the time he arrived in New Zealand and was in even better shape when he reached London.

Shackleton’s diaries show that he felt a mix of

: frustration, embarrassment and disappointment. He had been desperate to stay another winter and see the expedition through to its finish.

Yet studying this period, what

me was how Shackleton took advantage of his early return to Britain.

As the only officer back from Antarctica, he was in a unique position to tell the public and the media what had happened on their journey. He wrote articles for The Illustrated London News and Pearson’s Magazine and gave

to enthralled audiences, eager to hear about his amazing journey towards the South Pole.

Shackleton was also involved in equipping a relief vessel, the Dundee whaler Terra Nova, to help free the

from the ice the following year. By early 1904, he’d even managed to land a job as secretary of the Royal Scottish Geographical Society.

The Discovery expedition transformed Shackleton from an unknown officer in the

Navy into one of the best-known polar explorers in Britain. He’d also built a wealth of logistical experience and connections that left him perfectly placed to launch an expedition of his own – which he did in 1907, much to Scott’s

.

In his return to London, Shackleton had demonstrated his unique ability to make the very best of a disaster.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Objects found at a medieval Irish fort reveal details of daily life and material culture.
Horror filmmakers exploit features of human vision to create frightening effects.
Shackleton transformed Antarctic disappointment into a source of public fame.
Foley artists create carefully performed sound effects that play an essential role in cinema.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: Yet had you known Shackleton in 1895, his future fame as an Antarctic explorer would have seemed highly unlikely.

questions.prompt: What does the author argue about Shackleton's fame?
options: It depended exclusively on events on the ice.
It had no connection with public responses in Britain.
It was already fully established before he had a polar career.
His activities at home mattered as well as his time in Antarctica.
